name: Bharavi
bio: Bharavi was a Sanskrit court poet of the 6th century AD. An inscription of 634 AD at Aihole, which praises Kalidasa and Bharavi together, gives the latest date for him; tradition connects him with the Pallava and Western Ganga courts of southern India.

He is known for a single work, the Kiratarjuniya, an epic in eighteen cantos on the episode from the Mahabharata in which Arjuna, practising austerities, fights a hunter who is the god Shiva in disguise. Admired for its dense, ornate style and its mastery of metre, it became one of the six great mahakavyas of Sanskrit tradition. Here the first canto appears in the original Sanskrit.
